summary: This step ran a graph walk over PrimeKG v2.1 (a public biomedical knowledge graph, 129,375 nodes and 8,100,498 edges) from PrimeKG's grouped MVA disease node, which links five genes: BUB1, BUB1B, BUB3, CEP57 and TRIP13. The walk follows three metapaths (path templates: disease to gene to drug, through one protein-protein edge, or through a shared pathway), scores each drug as the sum over its paths of the product of 1/degree, and keeps drugs that carry a US label on openFDA. It found 4,265 paths to 745 drugs and kept 100 approved ones; no direct path exists, because PrimeKG has no drug edge on any of the five genes. The top five are fostamatinib, theophylline, NADH, pyridoxal phosphate and copper; BUB1B carries 18 % of the top-20 weight. The same walk from a decoy disease (XDH, xanthinuria) shares 2 of its top 20 drugs, and 6 of the real walk's top 20 are in iteration 2's drug_candidates.tsv. The GNN half of the goal (TxGNN) was skipped by user decision on 2026-09-23.
why: A drug ranking from a graph is only worth reading if it changes when the disease changes; otherwise it ranks drugs by how connected they are, not by the mechanism. The decoy walk (same code, a disease with no mitosis or checkpoint role, chosen by plan rule O6 and checked in PrimeKG itself) turns the ranking into a test rather than a demonstration. Comparing against iteration 2's literature/API-derived candidate list asks whether an independent method lands on the same drugs.
verdict: H074 (P4-11) supported at 0.75: overlap with the decoy's top 20 is 2 (NADH, pyridoxal phosphate), under the pre-registered 5 and unchanged with rank-20 ties. It is held below the suggested 0.83 because the decoy's neighbourhood has about 38 times fewer paths (113 vs 4,265), so a low overlap is partly guaranteed by construction, and both shared drugs are promiscuous cofactors. H075 (P4-12) supported at 0.45: 6 of the top 20 are in drug_candidates.tsv, over the pre-registered 2. But the decoy walk matches 7, so the list is broad enough that any walk passes; the claim had no power to show agreement on the mechanism, recorded as a refuting evidence row rather than re-scored. The walk vs GNN question is unanswered. The weighing is a transparent heuristic for triage, not a calibrated posterior.

inherits.what: No iteration-4 step feeds this one: the walk reads only the disease id from mechanism card v5, so it inherits the diagnosis, not the zoo's allele consensus (refuted at step 6). It reuses iteration 2's Track 2 inputs: the card, the XDH decoy card, the openFDA approval test, and drug_candidates.tsv as the comparison list.

hands_to.what: Nothing in iteration 4 reads step 7's ranking. It hands Track 2 a second, graph-derived candidate list with full lineage (ranking-walk.tsv, its paths, and a decoy baseline), plus two gaps to close: the walk does not penalise promiscuous drugs, and the card's HPO list misses the clinical file's eighth term.

figures.name: track2-walk-overlap.svg
figures.reads: Panel A splits each walk's top-20 distinct approved names into three parts: also in drug_candidates.tsv (blue: 6 for the MVA walk, 7 for the XDH decoy), shared with the other walk (yellow: 2 and 2), and neither (grey: 10 and 11); the dashed line is H075's threshold of 2. Panel B shows which of the five MVA genes carries the walk's top-20 path weight: BUB1 26.4 %, BUB3 23.6 %, TRIP13 18.5 %, BUB1B 18.1 % (green, the child's gene), CEP57 13.5 %.
figures.means: Panel A is the evidence that P4-12 had no power: the decoy clears the threshold by more than the real walk, so meeting it says nothing about the mechanism, while the small yellow segment is P4-11's support. Panel B shows the ranking is not BUB1B-specific: four of five start genes are not the child's and each carries a comparable share.
